name: Tai Hongjin
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Zhou Yaowen & Luo Meizhen 2001 (Dai dialect study covering Hongjin Dai), cited on Glottolog taih1246; no online copy reachable

sources.citation: Gao, Katie B. 2017. Dynamics of Language Contact in China: Ethnolinguistic Diversity and Variation in Yunnan. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 152 pp. hdl:10125/62498
sources.note: Nothing. Section 2.4.4 'Tai Hongjin (Dai)' (pp. 36-37) is a demolinguistic note on the Yongwu-cluster Tai of Tianxin, Dongpo and Jiyi townships, Wuding County (classified per Zhou & Luo 2001); the only Tai data are a 283-word wordlist (appendix; audio KG2-021 on Kaipuleohone). No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the text layer.

sources.citation: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat. 2009. The Phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University. hdl:1813/13855
sources.note: Nothing about Tai Hongjin: no Hongjin, Yuanjiang, Wuding or Maguan data point occurs in the text; stress is discussed only for the reconstructed Proto-Tai sesquisyllabic word (unstressed minor syllable + stressed major syllable), not for any modern Dai variety.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page for taih1246 (Tai Hongjin), with its reference list (Luo & Zhou 2001; Edmondson 2008; Luo 1987; Gao 2017; etc.)
sources.note: Nothing; confirms taih1246 (tiz) is a sister of Tai Ya (taiy1242, cuu) under 'Wuding-Yuanyang Tai', and that no reference is typed grammar or phonology (n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0).

sources.citation: Luo Meizhen. 1987. The evolution of vowel length and final consonants in Dai. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 10(1): 175-181. doi:10.15144/LTBA-10.1.175
sources.note: Nothing. A historical-phonology article on vowel length and final consonants with data from Wuding (Suosuoka, Wande commune), Yongren (Huiba, Yongxin commune) and Luchun (Qimaba commune) Dai, all tiz points, alongside Banna, Dehong and Jinping. The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur in the scanned text; tones are cited only by number.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Tai Hongjin language' (redirects to 'Tai Ya language'); Wikipedia (zh) 红金傣语
sources.note: Nothing on stress; en article gives consonant inventories for Yuanyang, Maguan, Wuding, Mosha and Yuanjiang dialects (unsourced beyond Zhou 2001) and lists the five Hongjin dialect areas (Yuanxin, Yongwu, Maguan, Yuanjiang, Lüshi) after Zhou (2001:14); zh article cites only Xing 1989 and Zhou 2001. Used for bibliography, not as a source.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2008. Shan and other Northern Tier Southeast Tai languages of Myanmar and China: Themes and Variations. In A. V. N. Diller, J. A. Edmondson & Luo Yongxian (eds), The Tai-Kadai Languages, 184-206. London: Routledge.

sources.access_detail: Harvard print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID WID-LC PL4113.T35 2008 (also: publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: English comparative overview whose data points include Tai-Yuanjiang (Dai La) and Tai-Wuding; may contain a general prosody remark for the Northern Tier varieties (final-syllable prominence in compounds) applying to Hongjin Dai.

sources.citation: Dao Chenghua 刀承华. 2008. 马关傣族 (The Dai of Maguan). Kunming: Yunnan Minzu Chubanshe.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Ethnography with a Maguan Dai (tiz) wordlist and possibly a brief phonology sketch; the only book-length work on the Maguan dialect area.

sources.citation: Luo Meizhen 罗美珍 & Zhou Yaowen 周耀文. 2001. 傣语方言研究：语音、词汇、文字 (A study of Dai dialects: phonology, lexicon, script). Beijing: Minzu Chubanshe. 400 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only full modern description covering the tiz points Wuding, Yuanjiang, Maguan and Luchun (plus Yuanyang = cuu); its 语音 (phonology) chapters are where a Chinese-academy statement on 重音 (stress) or its absence would be, and it is the source the earlier world scan and Glottolog both name. Print only; not on archive.org, HathiTrust or Google Books preview.

sources.citation: Zhou Yaowen 周耀文 & Luo Meizhen 罗美珍. 2001/2006. 傣语方言研究（语法） (A study of Dai dialects: grammar). Beijing: Minzu Chubanshe.

sources.note: Companion grammar volume to the 2001 phonology volume, listed in the held Glottolog bibliography; grammar volumes in this series sometimes repeat the prosodic word description (compounds, reduplication, weak syllables).
